chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, regarding the supplication for the child.

He said: Pour upon yourself a bucket from the water of Zamzam, then enter the House. So when you stand at the door of the House, take the ring of the door, then say: 'O Allah, the House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and You have said: 'And whoever enters it shall be secure', therefore secure me from Your punishment, and rescue me from Your wrath.'

Then enter the House, so perform two rak'at of prayer upon the red marble slab. Then stand before the pillar which is opposite the Stone, and press your chest against it, then say: 'O One, O the Alone, O the Glorious, O the Near, O the Remote, O the Mighty, O the Wise, Do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors, Endow to me from Yourself a goodly offspring. You are the Hearer of the supplication.'
Then circle by the pillar, and press your back and belly against it, and supplicate with this supplication. So if Allah wills something, it will happen.
ai.seo_question: What is the ritual supplication for having children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This supplication, transmitted via Safwan ibn Yahya in Al-Kafi, outlines a specific ritual for seeking offspring by combining physical acts of devotion—such as pressing against the pillar opposite the Black Stone—with recitation of divine attributes like 'Al-Wahid' and 'Al-Ahad'. It reflects the Shia emphasis on linking Quranic promises of divine protection and responsiveness to tangible acts of worship within the sanctity of the Kaaba.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

‘Regarding a supplication for the child, heasws said: ‘Pour upon yourself a cup from the water of Zamzam, then enter the House (Kabah). So when you stand upon the Door of the Kabah, so grab a ring of the Door, then say, ‘O Allahazwj! The House is Yourazwj House, and the servant is Yourazwj servant, and Youazwj have Said [3:97] and whoever enters it shall be secure, therefore Secure me from Yourazwj Punishment, and Resuce me from Yourazwj Wrath’.

Then enter the House (Kabah), so perform Salaat upon the red marble slab. Then arise to go to the Pillar which is parallel to the (Black) Stone, and adhere your chest with it, then say, ‘O the Alone! O the One! O the Glorious! O the Near One! O the Remote One! O the Mighty! O the Wise! [21:89] Lord! Do not leave me alone; and You are the Best of inheritors, Endow to me, from Youazwj, a goodly offspring. Youazwj are the Hearer of the supplications’.
Then circle by the Pillars, and adhere your back with it, and your belly, and supplicate with this supplication. So if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Wants something, it would happen’.
en.sarwar: Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar about prayer for children in a mawquf manner the following: “He (the Imam) has said, Tour on yourself a bucket of water from Zamzam, then enter the House. When you are at the door of the House, hold to the ring of the door and say, “O Allah, the House is Your house, the servant is Your servant and You have said, ‘Whoever enters it is safe/ so grant me immunity against Your torment and grant me refuge against Your anger.”

Thereafter enter the house and perform two Rak‘at salat (prayer) on the red marble. Go to the pillar next to the Black Stone, place your chest against it and say, “O the One, the Only One, O Glorious, O Near, O Far, O Majestic, O Wise, do not leave me alone. You are the best heir. Grant me virtuous children; You listen to appeals.”
Go around the pillar, place your back, belly against it, and say the prayer mentioned above again. If Allah wills something, it happens/”
